title: Chicken, NS as part, rotisserie, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide. In this case it refers to the “NS” part prepared on a rotisserie, with the skin left on and considered edible. This method keeps the meat juicy while the skin becomes crispy and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rotisserie cooking distributes heat evenly, resulting in tender meat.
Chicken skin contains beneficial fats that can be part of a balanced diet when cooked properly.
Rotisserie chicken is a tradition in many cultures, from Mediterranean to Asian cuisines.
The “NS” chicken cut is often used in fast‑food and street‑food dishes.
When marinated and roasted correctly, the skin can be a source of vitamin E.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat in lean meat
items.content: Skin‑less chicken breast contains very little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken is high in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones and immune health.

items.title: Beneficial fats in the skin
items.content: When eaten in moderation, chicken skin provides monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol in the skin
items.content: Chicken skin contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should limit intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: High sodium in prepared products
items.content: Pre‑marinated rotisserie chickens often contain added salt; check labels if you monitor sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rotisserie “NS” chicken can be served hot, sliced into pieces, added to salads, sandwiches, or enjoyed as a standalone snack. The skin can be eaten together with the meat for added crunch and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it remains good for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consumption.
